channel.title: Hacker News posts on daily.dev
channel.description: Hacker News is a community-driven platform for sharing and discussing technology news, startups, and programming-related topics. Through user submissions and comments, Hacker News offers insights into emerging technology trends, industry developments, and entrepreneurial ventures. Readers can participate in discussions, share their insights, and stay informed about the latest advancements in technology and innovation. - Powered by RSSHub

item.title: The Trackers and SDKs in ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Perplexity – James O'Claire
item.description: Analysis of third-party SDKs and APIs used by major AI chat applications (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Perplexity) on Android, revealing their development tools, analytics platforms, and monetization strategies. The research shows these apps primarily use Kotlin for development, integrate multiple analytics services like Google Analytics and Statsig, and employ various monetization tools including RevenueCat for subscription management and Stripe for payments.

item.title: robertjakob/rigorous: A comprehensive suite of tools, built to liberate science by making the creation, evaluation, and dissemination of research more...
item.description: Rigorous is an open-source AI-powered tool suite designed to automate scientific manuscript analysis and peer review. The main component, Agent1_Peer_Review, uses specialized AI agents to provide comprehensive manuscript evaluation, detailed feedback on scientific rigor and writing quality, and generates professional PDF reports. A cloud version offers free manuscript analysis with 1-2 day turnaround. The project aims to make scientific publishing more transparent, affordable, and efficient by leveraging AI for quality assessment and review automation.

item.title: Webb telescope helps refine Hubble constant, suggesting resolution to long-standing expansion rate debate
item.description: Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope have refined measurements of the Hubble constant, finding a value of 70.4 km/s/Mpc that aligns with cosmic microwave background measurements. This suggests resolution to a decade-long debate about conflicting universe expansion rates and supports the Standard Model of cosmology. Webb's superior resolution and sensitivity allow more accurate distance measurements by seeing through cosmic dust and identifying individual stars previously obscured.

item.title: volution/punchcard-key-backup: pckb -- backing up 128 bits into physical medium
item.description: A tool for backing up 128-bit cryptographic keys to physical punch cards using aluminum sheets. The system converts digital data to a hole-punching pattern that can be created at home with basic tools and recovered using the same web interface. Includes CRC error checking and supports various output formats including hexadecimal and text representation.

item.title: A Lean companion to “Analysis I”
item.description: Terence Tao has created a Lean companion to his real analysis textbook "Analysis I", translating definitions, theorems, and exercises into the Lean proof assistant. The project provides an alternative way to work through the book's exercises by filling in "sorries" in Lean code. Currently covering sections on natural numbers, addition, multiplication, set theory, and integers, the formalization bridges custom constructions with Mathlib's standard library. The companion serves both as a real analysis resource and an introduction to Lean and formal verification.

item.title: (lambda (x) (create x))
item.description: A developer shares their experience dealing with aggressive bot traffic that overwhelmed their personal server hosting git repositories and blog content. The post details how major companies like Amazon, Facebook, and OpenAI were scraping content without permission, causing resource exhaustion. The solution involved implementing nginx rate limiting, user agent blocking, and fail2ban automation to reject unwanted traffic, ultimately banning over 735 IP addresses. The author provides specific configuration examples and log analysis techniques using tools like lnav and goaccess.

item.title: Precision Clock Mk IV
item.description: A detailed technical breakdown of designing a GPS-synchronized precision clock with millisecond accuracy, featuring an articulated hinge design that transforms between single and dual-line displays. The project incorporates automatic timezone detection using GPS coordinates and shapefile data, implements a sophisticated bootloader system for firmware updates, and uses voltage-controlled LED brightness with buffer chips. Key challenges included managing multiple processors across the hinge connection with only four wires, implementing timezone database parsing on a microcontroller, and achieving sub-microsecond display synchronization.

item.title: AtomVM
item.description: AtomVM is a lightweight implementation of the Erlang BEAM virtual machine designed for IoT devices and microcontrollers. It supports a functional subset of BEAM opcodes and Erlang/OTP libraries, enabling developers to write IoT applications in Erlang or Elixir using actor-based concurrency. The platform includes advanced features like process spawning, message passing, preemptive scheduling, and garbage collection, while supporting hardware interfaces like GPIO, I2C, SPI, UART, and WiFi on devices like the ESP32.

item.title: Gradients are the new intervals
item.description: Researchers at IRIT and Adobe Research developed a new approach for optimizing signed distance field (SDF) rendering using Lipschitz continuity properties instead of traditional interval arithmetic. The method uses single-point evaluation with gradient bounds to create "pseudo-intervals" that can prune inactive primitives and perform far-field culling. While this approach is computationally cheaper and avoids issues with stacked transforms that plague interval arithmetic, it requires distance fields to maintain Lipschitz continuity. For non-compliant fields, normalization techniques can be applied before min/max operations to preserve the required properties, though this changes numerical values while preserving signs for CSG operations.

item.title: Virtual Threads Ate My Memory: A Web Crawler’s Tale of Speed vs. Memory
item.description: A developer's experience building a web crawler shows how switching from platform threads to Virtual Threads dramatically improved URL processing speed but caused OutOfMemoryError due to lack of backpressure. Virtual Threads removed I/O bottlenecks, allowing rapid parallel downloads that overwhelmed memory with pending results. Solutions include using semaphores to limit concurrency and implementing rate limiting. The key lesson is that Virtual Threads require explicit resource management since traditional thread limits no longer provide implicit backpressure.
